apis.name: LoadLibraryW
apis.summary: Loads a module into the address space of the calling process.
apis.description: LoadLibraryW maps a module into the calling process and prepares it for execution, resolving its static imports when the image is loaded as an executable module. If the module is already loaded, the system returns its handle and increments the per-process reference count, so each successful call should be balanced by a call to FreeLibrary. When the name is not a fully qualified path, the loader uses its documented search order, which means the directory a module is loaded from depends on process configuration and loader settings.
apis.prototype: HMODULE LoadLibraryW(LPCWSTR lpLibFileName);

parameters.name: lpLibFileName
parameters.description: The file name of the module to load. If the name omits a path, the loader searches the documented DLL search path. If the extension is omitted, .dll is appended unless the name ends with a period. When specifying a path, use backslashes rather than forward slashes.

return.success: A handle to the loaded module. The handle remains valid until the module is unloaded.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError for the loader error, which may describe a missing module or a failed dependency.

apis.unicode_notes: LoadLibraryW is the Unicode variant. LoadLibraryA accepts an ANSI file name, and the encoding-neutral LoadLibrary alias resolves to one of them at compile time based on UNICODE.
apis.remarks: Each successful call increments the module's per-process reference count; call FreeLibrary once for each successful load. Do not call LoadLibrary from DllMain, because doing so can deadlock on the loader lock. A module loaded with LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE through LoadLibraryExW is not an executable image and is not returned by GetModuleHandleW.
apis.maldev_notes: Dynamic module loading is routine in plugin hosts, language runtimes, installers, and software that defers optional functionality until it is needed. Analysts also encounter it in code that resolves functionality at run time. The module path, the search-order context, and any subsequent export lookups are more informative than the call itself.
apis.defensive_notes: Module-load telemetry, including image-load events where the platform exposes them, can show which module was mapped, from which path, and by which process. Modules loaded from user-writable directories or lacking a valid signature deserve review, but a load event alone does not establish intent.

example.title: Load a system DLL and resolve one export
example.notes: Illustrative only. The example loads a signed system DLL, resolves one documented export, and releases the load with FreeLibrary. It does not handle modules obtained from untrusted paths.

apis.source_notes: Prototype, search-order behavior, and reference-count semantics checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.name: LoadLibraryExW
apis.summary: Loads a module with additional loader options that control initialization and search behavior.
apis.description: LoadLibraryExW is a generalized form of LoadLibraryW. The dwFlags value selects behaviors such as mapping a file as data instead of executing it, restricting the directories searched for the module and its dependencies, or requiring a signed target at load time. A dwFlags value of zero reproduces LoadLibraryW behavior. The optional data-file modes are useful for reading resources without running the image's initialization code.
apis.prototype: HMODULE LoadLibraryExW(LPCWSTR lpLibFileName, HANDLE hFile, DWORD dwFlags);

parameters.name: lpLibFileName
parameters.description: The file name of the module to load. A fully qualified path limits the search to that path. If the name omits a path and the extension, the loader appends .dll unless the name ends with a period.

parameters.name: hFile
parameters.description: Reserved for future use. It must be NULL.

parameters.name: dwFlags
parameters.description: Flags that control how the module is loaded and located, such as LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE, LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_IMAGE_RESOURCE, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32, or LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS. Zero gives the same behavior as LoadLibraryW.

return.success: A handle to the loaded module. Handles returned by this function can be passed to FreeLibrary.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError for the loader error.

apis.unicode_notes: LoadLibraryExW is the Unicode variant. LoadLibraryExA accepts an ANSI file name, and the encoding-neutral LoadLibraryEx alias resolves to one of them at compile time.
apis.remarks: Modules loaded with LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE or LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_IMAGE_RESOURCE are not visible to GetModuleHandleW and cannot be used with GetProcAddress. FreeLibrary should still be called for handles returned by LoadLibraryExW, whether or not the load incremented the reference count. The LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_* flags require the documented update on Windows 7, Windows Server 2008 R2, Windows Vista, and Windows Server 2008; callers that need them on those versions should verify support at run time.
apis.maldev_notes: The data-file and search-path flags matter in analysis because they change whether code runs and where dependencies are resolved. Data-file loading is a normal way to inspect resources without executing an image, while explicit search flags are a documented way to avoid unsafe directories. The flags describe intent only in combination with the path and subsequent behavior.
apis.defensive_notes: Loader telemetry may not expose the flags directly; investigators often reconstruct behavior from the module path, whether DllMain ran, and which dependencies were mapped. Signed-target enforcement and system-directory search are relevant when reviewing how a process resists DLL search-order manipulation.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, flag meanings, and data-file reference-count behavior checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.name: GetProcAddress
apis.summary: Retrieves the address of an exported function or variable from a loaded module.
apis.description: GetProcAddress resolves an export by name or ordinal in a module that is already loaded in the calling process. The returned address is valid only while the module remains loaded. The export name is an ANSI string even in a Unicode build; the function has no W variant. Callers typically cast the returned FARPROC to the function pointer type declared by the export's documentation.
apis.prototype: FARPROC GetProcAddress(HMODULE hModule, LPCSTR lpProcName);

parameters.name: hModule
parameters.description: A handle to the loaded module that contains the export. The handle can come from LoadLibraryW, LoadLibraryExW, GetModuleHandleW, or the process image. Modules loaded as data files cannot be used.

parameters.name: lpProcName
parameters.description: The exported function or variable name as a narrow, case-sensitive string, or an ordinal placed in the low word of a MAKEINTRESOURCEA value.

return.success: The address of the exported function or variable.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError; ERROR_PROC_NOT_FOUND indicates that the export was not found.

apis.unicode_notes: GetProcAddress has no Unicode variant and takes an LPCSTR export name. The narrow export name must be used even in a Unicode build; the -W suffix does not apply to this function.
apis.remarks: Cast the result to the correct function pointer type before calling it. A signature or calling-convention mismatch is undefined behavior. The address must not be used after the owning module has been unloaded. Ordinal-based lookup is supported but is less portable than lookup by name.
apis.maldev_notes: Run-time export resolution appears in plugin systems, delayed-loading implementations, compatibility shims, and software that supports multiple operating-system versions. Analysts often inspect the resolved names because they reveal capability that is absent from the static import table, while the resolution mechanism itself is a general-purpose technique.
apis.defensive_notes: Exports resolved at run time do not appear in a module's static import table, so import-table review alone can miss them. String, memory, and API-monitoring telemetry often provide the complementary view. The resolved name and the module it came from are usually more useful than the resolution call.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, ANSI-only export name, and module-lifetime notes checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.name: GetModuleHandleW
apis.summary: Returns a handle to a module already loaded in the calling process.
apis.description: GetModuleHandleW looks up a module that is already mapped in the calling process. Passing NULL returns a handle to the executable image of the calling process. The function does not load the module and does not increment its reference count, so the returned handle must not be passed to FreeLibrary. Its result can become stale if another thread unloads the module.
apis.prototype: HMODULE GetModuleHandleW(LPCWSTR lpModuleName);

parameters.name: lpModuleName
parameters.description: The name of the loaded module, with or without a path. If the extension is omitted, .dll is appended unless the name ends with a period. NULL requests the handle of the executable file used to create the calling process.

return.success: A handle to the specified loaded module, or to the calling process's executable when lpModuleName is NULL.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError; the module is not loaded or the name did not resolve.

apis.unicode_notes: GetModuleHandleW is the Unicode variant. GetModuleHandleA accepts an ANSI module name, and the encoding-neutral GetModuleHandle alias resolves to one of them at compile time.
apis.remarks: The returned handle is not global or inheritable and cannot be duplicated into another process. Do not pass it to FreeLibrary: although the lookup did not increment the reference count, FreeLibrary would decrement it and could unmap the module prematurely. GetModuleHandleEx offers flags that keep a module loaded and is safer when the handle must remain valid across threads.
apis.maldev_notes: Code frequently calls GetModuleHandleW(NULL) to locate its own image, or checks whether a module is already present before loading it. Both patterns are ordinary, and analysts use them to reconstruct module dependencies and self-referential path logic.
apis.defensive_notes: The call is local to the process and does not create a kernel object, so it generates little dedicated telemetry. Interpretation depends on the requested module and on what the program does with the handle.
apis.source_notes: NULL-handle behavior, data-file limitation, and reference-count caveat checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.name: FreeLibrary
apis.summary: Decrements a loaded module's reference count and unloads it when the count reaches zero.
apis.description: FreeLibrary releases a reference obtained from LoadLibraryW or LoadLibraryExW. When the per-process reference count reaches zero, the system calls the module's DllMain with DLL_PROCESS_DETACH and unmaps the module. A handle returned by GetModuleHandleW does not carry a new reference and must not be passed to FreeLibrary.
apis.prototype: BOOL FreeLibrary(HMODULE hLibModule);

parameters.name: hLibModule
parameters.description: A handle to the loaded module library. It must have been returned by LoadLibraryW or LoadLibraryExW, and each successful load should be released exactly once.

return.success: A nonzero value; the reference count was decremented.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: Unloading a module invalidates every address previously obtained from GetProcAddress for that module. Loader functions, including FreeLibrary, should not be called from DllMain because of loader-lock deadlock risk. Do not free a handle obtained from GetModuleHandleW.
apis.maldev_notes: Explicit unloads appear in plugin hosts and in code that uses a module only temporarily. Module lifetime is more often relevant to reconstructing program flow than to classifying behavior.
apis.defensive_notes: Module-unload telemetry can explain gaps in later image-load records and is best correlated with the process's module history. An unload followed by a load from a different path can be worth reviewing.
apis.source_notes: Reference-count and unload semantics checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.name: GetModuleFileNameW
apis.summary: Retrieves the fully qualified path of the file that contains a loaded module.
apis.description: GetModuleFileNameW copies the path of a module loaded in the calling process into a caller-supplied buffer. Passing NULL for hModule requests the path of the executable image. The returned string uses the same form in which the module was loaded, so it can contain a short (8.3) name or a \\?\ prefix.
apis.prototype: DWORD GetModuleFileNameW(HMODULE hModule, LPWSTR lpFilename, DWORD nSize);

parameters.name: hModule
parameters.description: A handle to the loaded module whose path is requested. NULL requests the path of the executable file of the calling process. Modules loaded with LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE are not covered.

parameters.name: lpFilename
parameters.description: A buffer that receives the path as a null-terminated string when the buffer is large enough.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.description: The size of the lpFilename buffer, in WCHARs. If the path is too long for the buffer, it is truncated to nSize characters including the terminating null character on Windows Vista and later.

return.success: The number of characters copied to the buffer, not including the terminating null character. A return value equal to nSize indicates that the path may have been truncated.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.unicode_notes: GetModuleFileNameW is the Unicode variant and reports the buffer size in WCHARs. GetModuleFileNameA accepts a byte buffer, and the encoding-neutral GetModuleFileName alias resolves to one of them at compile time.
apis.remarks: Do not assume a path that fills the buffer is complete; allocate a larger buffer and retry when the return value equals nSize. The function reports the path associated with the loaded module, which may differ in case, name form, or prefix from the path on disk.
apis.maldev_notes: Programs use their own module path to locate configuration, resources, or sibling files. In analysis the same call can show where an image was executed from, which is useful context but not a behavioral indicator by itself.
apis.defensive_notes: Process image-path telemetry already covers the main executable; this API matters mostly for non-main modules and for understanding path-dependent behavior such as loading files relative to the module.

example.title: Print the path of the current executable
example.notes: Illustrative only. The example requests the current executable's path and treats a full buffer as a possible truncation rather than using the string unconditionally.

apis.source_notes: Prototype, WCHAR buffer sizing, and truncation return-value behavior checked against Microsoft Learn (libloaderapi.h).

apis.dll: Kernel32.dll on Windows 7 and Windows Server 2008 R2; Psapi.dll (if PSAPI_VERSION=1) on Windows 7 and Windows Server 2008 R2; Psapi.dll on Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista, Windows Server 2003 and Windows XP

apis.summary: Retrieves a handle for each module in the specified process.
apis.description: Retrieves a handle for each module in the specified process. To control whether a 64-bit application enumerates 32-bit modules, 64-bit modules, or both types of modules, use the EnumProcessModulesEx function.
apis.prototype: BOOL EnumProcessModules(HANDLE hProcess, HMODULE* lphModule, DWORD cb, LPDWORD lpcbNeeded);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the process.

parameters.name: lphModule
parameters.description: An array that receives the list of module handles.

parameters.name: cb
parameters.description: The size of the lphModule array, in bytes.

parameters.name: lpcbNeeded
parameters.description: The number of bytes required to store all module handles in the lphModule array.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The EnumProcessModules function is primarily designed for use by debuggers and similar applications that must extract module information from another process. If the module list in the target process is corrupted or not yet initialized, or if the module list changes during the function call as a result of DLLs being loaded or unloaded, EnumProcessModules may fail or return incorrect information. It is a good idea to specify a large array of HMODULE values, because it is hard to predict how many modules there will be in the process at the time you call EnumProcessModules. To determine if the lphModule array is too small to hold all module handles for the process, compare the value returned in lpcbNeeded with the value specified in cb. If lpcbNeeded is greater than cb, increase the size of the array and call EnumProcessModules again. To determine how many modules were enumerated by the call to EnumProcessModules, divide the resulting value in the lpcbNeeded parameter by sizeof(HMODULE). The EnumProcessModules function does not retrieve handles for modules that were loaded with the LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE or similar flags. For more information, see LoadLibraryEx. Do not call CloseHandle on any of the handles returned by this function. The information comes from a snapshot, so there are no resources to be freed. apis.name: EnumResourceTypesA
apis.summary: Enumerates resource types within a binary module.
apis.description: Enumerates resource types within a binary module. Starting with Windows Vista, this is typically a language-neutral Portable Executable (LN file), and the enumeration also includes resources from one of the corresponding language-specific resource files (.mui files)—if one exists—that contain localizable language resources. It is also possible to use hModule to specify a .mui file, in which case only that file is searched for resource types. Alternately, applications can call EnumResourceTypesEx, which provides more precise control over which resource files to enumerate.
apis.prototype: BOOL EnumResourceTypesA(HMODULE hModule, ENUMRESTYPEPROCA lpEnumFunc, LONG_PTR lParam);

parameters.name: hModule
parameters.description: This handle must be obtained through LoadLibrary or LoadLibraryEx. See Remarks for more information. If this parameter is NULL, that is equivalent to passing in a handle to the module used to create the current process.

parameters.name: lpEnumFunc
parameters.description: For more information, see the EnumResTypeProc function.

parameters.name: lParam
parameters.description: The lParam parameter for EnumResourceTypesA, as documented by the API reference.

return.success: See the reference for the documented success value.
return.failure: Returns TRUE if successful or FALSE if the function does not find a resource, if the enumeration has been stopped, or if the function fails for another reason. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: For each resource type found, EnumResourceTypes calls an application-defined callback function lpEnumFunc, passing each resource type it finds, as well as the various other parameters that were passed to EnumResourceTypes. EnumResourceTypes continues to enumerate resource types until the callback function returns FALSE or all resource types have been enumerated. Starting with Windows Vista, if hModule specifies an LN file, then the types enumerated correspond to resources that reside in the LN file and in the .mui file associated with it. If no .mui files are found, only types from the LN file are returned. The order in which .mui files are searched is the usual Resource Loader search order; see User Interface Language Management for details. After one appropriate .mui file is found, the search does not continue further to other .mui files associated with the LN file, because all .mui files that correspond to a single LN file have the same set of resource types. The enumeration never includes duplicates: if a given resource type is contained in both the LN file and in an .mui file, the type is enumerated only once. #### Examples For an example, see Creating a Resource List. > > The winbase.h header defines EnumResourceTypes as an alias that automatically selects the ANSI or Unicode version of this function based on the definition of the UNICODE preprocessor constant. apis.name: FindResourceA
apis.summary: Determines the location of a resource with the specified type and name in the specified module.
apis.description: Determines the location of a resource with the specified type and name in the specified module. To specify a language, use the FindResourceEx function.
apis.prototype: HRSRC FindResourceA(HMODULE hModule, LPCSTR lpName, LPCSTR lpType);

parameters.name: hModule
parameters.description: If this parameter is NULL, the function searches the module used to create the current process.

parameters.name: lpName
parameters.description: Alternately, rather than a pointer, this parameter can be MAKEINTRESOURCE(ID), where ID is the integer identifier of the resource. For more information, see the Remarks section below.

parameters.name: lpType
parameters.description: Alternately, rather than a pointer, this parameter can be MAKEINTRESOURCE(ID), where ID is the integer identifier of the given resource type. For standard resource types, see Resource Types. For more information, see the Remarks section below.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is a handle to the specified resource's information block. To obtain a handle to the resource, pass this handle to the LoadResource function.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: If IS_INTRESOURCE is TRUE for x = lpName or lpType, x specifies the integer identifier of the name or type of the given resource. Otherwise, those parameters are long pointers to null-terminated strings. If the first character of the string is a pound sign (#), the remaining characters represent a decimal number that specifies the integer identifier of the resource's name or type. For example, the string "#258" represents the integer identifier 258. To reduce the amount of memory required for a resource, an application should refer to it by integer identifier instead of by name. An application can use FindResource to find any type of resource, but this function should be used only if the application must access the binary resource data by making subsequent calls to LoadResource and then to LockResource. parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the process that contains the module. The handle must have the PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION and PROCESS_VM_READ access rights. For more information, see Process Security and Access Rights.

parameters.description: A handle to the module. If this parameter is NULL, this function returns the name of the file used to create the calling process.

apis.remarks: The GetModuleBaseName function is primarily designed for use by debuggers and similar applications that must extract module information from another process. If the module list in the target process is corrupted or is not yet initialized, or if the module list changes during the function call as a result of DLLs being loaded or unloaded, GetModuleBaseName may fail or return incorrect information. To retrieve the base name of a module in the current process, use the GetModuleFileName function to retrieve the full module name and then use a function call such as strrchr(szmodulename, '\') to scan to the beginning of the base name within the module name string. This is more efficient and more reliable than calling GetModuleBaseName with a handle to the current process. To retrieve the base name of the main executable module for a remote process, use the GetProcessImageFileName or QueryFullProcessImageName function to retrieve the module name and then use the strrchr function as described in the previous paragraph. This is more efficient and more reliable than calling GetModuleBaseName with a NULL module handle. The GetModuleBaseName function does not retrieve the base name for modules that were loaded with the LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE flag. For more information, see LoadLibraryEx. apis.name: GetModuleFileNameA
apis.summary: Retrieves the fully qualified path for the file that contains the specified module.
apis.description: Retrieves the fully qualified path for the file that contains the specified module. The module must have been loaded by the current process. To locate the file for a module that was loaded by another process, use the GetModuleFileNameEx function.
apis.prototype: DWORD GetModuleFileNameA(HMODULE hModule, LPSTR lpFilename, DWORD nSize);

parameters.name: hModule
parameters.description: A handle to the loaded module whose path is being requested. If this parameter is NULL, GetModuleFileName retrieves the path of the executable file of the current process. The GetModuleFileName function does not retrieve the path for modules that were loaded using the LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE flag. For more information, see LoadLibraryEx.

parameters.name: lpFilename
parameters.description: A pointer to a buffer that receives the fully qualified path of the module. If the length of the path is less than the size that the nSize parameter specifies, the function succeeds and the path is returned as a null-terminated string. If the length of the path equals or exceeds the value specified by nSize, the function succeeds and the string is truncated to nSize characters (including the terminating null character). Windows XP: The string is truncated to nSize characters and is not null-terminated. The string returned will use the same format that was specified when the module was loaded. Therefore, the path can be a long or short file name, and can use the prefix \?\. For more information, see Naming a File.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.description: The size of the lpFilename buffer, in TCHARs.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is the length of the string that is copied to the buffer, in characters, not including the terminating null character. If the buffer is too small to hold the module name, the string is truncated to nSize characters including the terminating null character, the function returns nSize, and the function sets the last error to ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER.
return.failure: Windows XP: If the buffer is too small to hold the module name, the function returns nSize. The last error code remains ERROR_SUCCESS. If nSize is zero, the return value is zero and the last error code is ERROR_SUCCESS. If the function fails, the return value is 0 (zero). To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: If a DLL is loaded in two processes, its file name in one process may differ in case from its file name in the other process. The global variable _pgmptr is automatically initialized to the full path of the executable file, and can be used to retrieve the full path name of an executable file. #### Examples For an example, see Installing a Service. > > The libloaderapi.h header defines GetModuleFileName as an alias that automatically selects the ANSI or Unicode version of this function based on the definition of the UNICODE preprocessor constant. Mixing usage of the encoding-neutral alias with code that is not encoding-neutral can lead to mismatches that result in compilation or runtime errors. For more information, see Conventions for Function Prototypes.

apis.summary: Retrieves a module handle for the specified module.
apis.description: Retrieves a module handle for the specified module. The module must have been loaded by the calling process. To avoid the race conditions described in the Remarks section, use the GetModuleHandleEx function.

parameters.name: lpModuleName
parameters.description: The name of the loaded module (either a .dll or .exe file). If the file name extension is omitted, the default library extension .dll is appended. The file name string can include a trailing point character (.) to indicate that the module name has no extension. The string does not have to specify a path. When specifying a path, be sure to use backslashes (\), not forward slashes (/). The name is compared (case independently) to the names of modules currently mapped into the address space of the calling process. If this parameter is NULL, GetModuleHandle returns a handle to the file used to create the calling process (.exe file). The GetModuleHandle function does not retrieve handles for modules that were loaded using the LOAD_LIBRARY_AS_DATAFILE flag. For more information, see LoadLibraryEx.

The GetModuleHandle function returns a handle to a mapped module without incrementing its reference count. However, if this handle is passed to the FreeLibrary function, the reference count of the mapped module will be decremented. Therefore, do not pass a handle returned by GetModuleHandle to the FreeLibrary function. Doing so can cause a DLL module to be unmapped prematurely. This function must be used carefully in a multithreaded application. There is no guarantee that the module handle remains valid between the time this function returns the handle and the time it is used. For example, suppose that a thread retrieves a module handle, but before it uses the handle, a second thread frees the module. If the system loads another module, it could reuse the module handle that was recently freed.
